A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we establish completeness for all determinantal processes that we consider, with the exception of the continuum Airy kernel process, which we conjecture to be complete.
we provide the first nontrivial results on completeness for determinantal processes in the critical regime.
, under certain assumptions, completeness holds almost surely if and only if the underlying point process is ergodic and the corresponding determinantal measure is non-trivial.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the determinantal point process structure is a powerful tool to establish the critical case of completeness of random exponentals, and in particular that the critical case is not much more difficult than the subcritical case.
the completeness question is intimately linked to the asymptotic behaviour of the determinantal kernel, and in particular its decay rate at large distances.
the critical case of completeness for random determinantal processes is often the same as for the deterministic case.
